subject: Pilot conversion: legacy license -> metered consumption & platform fee allocation
messages:
From: Ana Rivera <ana.rivera@novapulse.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@novapulse.com
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot conversion: legacy license -> metered consumption & platform fee allocation

Jordan — thanks for the time earlier. We discussed moving our existing private deployment (3 sites, ~80 GPUs) from the legacy per-site license to a metered model tied to token consumption for inference, but the finance team is asking for clarity on two things before we take this to procurement: 1) how the platform fee is allocated against metered usage (is it a flat platform fee + per-token, or a creditable platform fee?), and 2) whether there are conversion credits / ETAs for the unused portion of our existing 24‑month license.

Can you confirm options and an example ARR comparison? I attached the current invoice summary. We need something concise to share with our CFO.

—Ana
Senior Eng Ops, Novapulse

Attachment: invoice_summary_Q1_2027.pdf (stub)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Ana Rivera <ana.rivera@novapulse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot conversion: legacy license -> metered consumption & platform fee allocation

Ana — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers up front, then I’ve attached a conversion worksheet for a worked example: 

1) Platform fee options for private deployments (we can do either):
   - Option A (Flat + metered): Fixed annual platform fee (example: $60k/year) + per‑token metered rate. Simpler for budgeting; platform fee not credited against consumption.
   - Option B (Creditable platform fee): Reduced annual platform fee (example: $25k/year) + higher per‑token rate, with an annual reconciliation where up to X% of platform fee is credited toward overage consumption (prorated monthly). Better for customers expecting variable consumption.

2) Conversion credit for legacy licenses: we typically offer a pro‑rata credit for remaining term of the legacy license against the first 12 months of committed metered usage. Standard credit ranges from 20–40% of remaining prepaid value depending on remaining term and whether they commit to a 12‑month consumption minimum.

Irene is looped in to confirm technical SOW impact and Marissa on commercial math — I also attached the conversion_workbook_v3.xlsx for your CFO with worked examples at 25% and 35% conversion credit.

Next steps: tell me which platform fee option you prefer and whether you’d consider a 12‑month minimum commitment to maximize credit. I can send a short SOW + amendment draft.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0198

Attachments: conversion_workbook_v3.xlsx, SOW_draft_20270605.pdf (stubs)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot conversion: legacy license -> metered consumption & platform fee allocation

Ana — quick commercial summary from our side (numbers illustrative; happy to lock after we confirm consumption profile):

Scenario 1 — Flat platform fee (Option A):
- Platform fee: $60,000 / year (covers control plane, console, SSO integrations, 30-day log retention)
- Metered rate: $0.0009 per token (generation+prompt)
- Conversion credit: 25% of remaining prepaid value applied to Year 1 committed consumption (assumes 12‑month minimum with monthly reconciliation)
- Estimated ARR (Year 1) w/ your current baseline consumption: $1.02M vs legacy annualized of $1.15M (savings in Year 1 after credit).

Scenario 2 — Creditable platform fee (Option B):
- Platform fee: $25,000 / year
- Metered rate: $0.0011 per token
- Credit mechanics: Platform fee up to 50% applied as monthly credits against overage if you exceed committed baseline; unused credits do not rollover beyond 12 months.
- Estimated ARR (Year 1): $1.10M with deeper upside if consumption grows >20% (because platform fee is partially creditable).

Tradeoffs: A is predictable for finance; B aligns cost with usage and makes growth cheaper.

If you want, Jordan and I can finalize a 1‑page cost comparison using your actual monthly token exports. Otherwise, state which scenario your CFO prefers and we’ll prepare contract language.

—Marissa
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: conversion_workbook_v3.xlsx (worked examples)

From: Ana Rivera <ana.rivera@novapulse.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot conversion: legacy license -> metered consumption & platform fee allocation

Thanks, Jordan & Marissa — this is helpful. A few quick responses from our CFO (copied):
- They prefer Option B (creditable platform fee) because Novapulse expects spikey workloads and wants protection vs fixed sunk fees.
- They asked whether the conversion credit can be increased to 35% if we agree to a 24‑month committed consumption minimum (vs your standard 12 months).
- Also requested a short clause that if we terminate early (after month 12) we receive a pro‑rata termination credit applied against the outstanding committed consumption (not to exceed remaining conversion credit amount).

Can you confirm Redwoods flexibility on the two asks? Ana

—Ana Rivera
Senior Eng Ops, Novapulse

Attachment: CFO_questions.pdf (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ana Rivera <ana.rivera@novapulse.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot conversion: legacy license -> metered consumption & platform fee allocation

Ana — appreciate the clarity. Internal confirmation below and next steps: 

1) 24‑month committed consumption minimum: we can accept a 35% conversion credit for the remaining prepaid value if Novapulse signs a 24‑month committed consumption agreement (minimum annual baseline agreed in SOW). We’ll document the baseline and monthly reconciliation in the SOW.

2) Early termination credit: we can include a limited early termination credit that is pro‑rata: after month 12, if Novapulse terminates, Redwood will apply a pro‑rata credit equal to the unused portion of the conversion credit against any termination liability, capped at the remaining conversion credit value. This is standard wording and still protects Redwood from short‑term churn while giving Novapulse downside protection.

3) Platform fee mechanics for Option B (creditable): we’ll specify in the SOW that up to 50% of paid platform fee can be applied as monthly credits against overage consumption in months where actual consumption exceeds committed baseline. Credits expire after 12 months and do not convert to cash.

Next steps: Jordan — can you send an updated SOW + amendment with: 24‑month baseline table, 35% conversion credit line item, early termination credit clause, and the platform fee credit table? I’ll approve the commercial markup and loop legal for redlines.

Ana — once we have your actual monthly token exports (1Q‑2Q 2027), we’ll finalize numbers and provide the signature‑ready amendment.

Thanks — Marissa
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference
